claim_reference: Adv. Funct. Mater. 2026, 36:e75639, Section 1, Section 2.1, Section 5 (High-Dimensional Active Learning Space Exploration)

preregistration.hypothesis: The 168 experimental formulations comprehensively explore the 5D parameter design space under the reported active learning campaigns.
preregistration.primary_metric: 5D Convex Hull volume as percentage of nominal box and percentage of physically feasible formulation domain.
preregistration.decision_rule: SUPPORTED if convex hull volume >= 20% of feasible parameter space; WEAKENED if convex hull volume < 10% of feasible space; CONTRADICTED if convex hull volume < 1% of feasible space.

summary: Geometric audit reveals that the 168 formulations explored only 2.815% of the nominal 5D box and 6.14% of the physically feasible domain, leaving 93.9% of the feasible formulation space completely untouched. The initial 100 closed-loop points occupied merely 0.436% of the box due to heavy spatial clustering along narrow rays. Consequently, active learning did not navigate the global 5D space but rather localized intensely within a tiny corner, explaining why simple response surface methods perform comparably.
